These features are more typical of aggressive IDH-wildtype diffuse glioma than of an IDH-mutant lower-grade phenotype. Overall the aggressive enhancement, necrosis, edema, and deep white-matter invasion outweigh the younger age and cortical/temporal involvement, so the best MRI-based estimate is IDH-wildtype.

However, the non-frontal temporal/deep distribution and aggressive enhancement/necrosis pattern make non-codeleted status the better estimate.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured conventional MRI metadata without diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, or susceptibility/calcification information. Molecular confirmation remains required; age and cortical temporal involvement leave some residual uncertainty, but the marked enhancement, necrosis, extensive edema, and deep white-matter involvement strongly suggest an aggressive adult-type diffuse glioma.

who_grade.reasoning: For CNS WHO grade considered independently, the MRI metadata strongly favor grade 4. Enhancement Quality, Thickness of enhancing margin, ET Volume (mL), and Proportion Enhancing show substantial marked enhancement; NCR Volume (mL) and Proportion Necrosis show necrotic/non-enhancing tumor component; ED Volume (mL) and Proportion of Oedema show extensive edema; Total tumor volume (mL), Lesion Sizes APxTVxCC (cm), and Deep WM invasion indicate a large infiltrative lesion. This combination is much more compatible with grade 4 than grade 2, and more aggressive than typical grade 3 imaging. Features arguing against the highest grade include midline_shift_present showing no midline shift, Asymmetrical Ventricles being absent, Multifocal or Multicentric being solitary, and Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion being absent. These do not outweigh the marked enhancement, necrosis, edema, and large infiltrative tumor burden, so grade 4 is the best MRI-based estimate.
